types.embedding_query_text: Person: A human being. Also called Individual, Human, Client, Customer, Employee. Examples: Sophia Laforteza, Manon Bannerman, Laforteza, vocalist.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org Person class directly matches the OIE_TYPE 'Person' and its definition, as well as the provided examples of individuals.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: PeopleAudience
candidates.comment: A PeopleAudience, as an Audience, describes a set of characteristics belonging to people, e.g., who compose an item's target audience. Also called demographic group, target audience, human audience. Examples: 'adults aged 18-35', 'students', 'retirees'. Distinct from Audience, which is a broader category including non-human audiences.

candidates.label: IndividualProduct
candidates.comment: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. Examples: a laptop with a specific serial number, a particular copy of a book, a unique piece of art. Distinct from ProductModel, which describes a class of products, and ProductGroup, which is a collection of products.

candidates.label: Audience
candidates.comment: An Audience is an Intangible entity representing the specific group of people for whom an item or creative work is intended. Also called target group, readership, viewership, demographic. Examples: children, teenagers, medical professionals, general public, investors.

candidates.label: Product
candidates.comment: A Product is any offered good or service. Also called item, merchandise, offering. Examples: a pair of shoes, a concert ticket, a car rental service, an episode of a TV show.

types.embedding_query_text: Girl Group: A musical group consisting of female vocalists. Also called Female Band, Pop Group, Vocal Ensemble, Music Group. Examples: Katseye, popular girl group, the ensemble, The girl group.

chosen_type.label: MusicGroup
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org MusicGroup class accurately describes a 'Girl Group' as an organization of musicians, fitting the example 'Katseye'.

candidates.label: MusicGroup
candidates.comment: A MusicGroup, as a PerformingGroup, is an organization of musicians, such as a band or orchestra, or a solo musician. Also called band, musical ensemble, orchestra, solo artist. Examples: The Beatles, New York Philharmonic, Taylor Swift. Distinct from PerformingGroup, which is a broader category for any performance group.

candidates.label: PerformingGroup
candidates.comment: A PerformingGroup is an organization of performers, such as a band, orchestra, or circus. Also called performance ensemble, troupe, artistic group. Examples: Cirque du Soleil, a local theatre company, a dance troupe. Distinct from MusicGroup, which is specifically for musical performers.

candidates.label: DanceGroup
candidates.comment: A DanceGroup is a performing organization specializing in dance, often presenting choreographed performances. Also called dance company, ballet troupe, dance ensemble, dance collective. Examples: Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater, Riverdance, New York City Ballet, Bolshoi Ballet.

candidates.label: TheaterGroup
candidates.comment: An organization or company dedicated to producing and performing theatrical works. Also called theater company, drama troupe, acting ensemble. Examples: The Royal Shakespeare Company, Cirque du Soleil, a local amateur dramatics society.

candidates.label: MusicAlbumProductionType
candidates.comment: MusicAlbumProductionType is an enumeration classifying a music album by its content type. Also called album type, production category. Examples: StudioAlbum, LiveAlbum, Soundtrack, CompilationAlbum. Distinct from MusicAlbumReleaseType, which describes the release format.

types.embedding_query_text: HealthCondition: A state of health that deviates from normal functioning, often requiring attention or care. Also called Illness, Ailment, Disorder, Medical Condition, Sickness. Examples: mental health concerns, health and wellbeing, mental health and wellness, her condition.

chosen_type.label: MedicalCondition
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org MedicalCondition class encompasses 'mental health concerns' and general 'health and wellbeing' issues that deviate from normal functioning.

candidates.label: MedicalCondition
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing any condition of the human body that affects normal functioning, including diseases, injuries, disabilities, and disorders. Also called disease, illness, health disorder, ailment. Examples: "influenza", "diabetes", "a broken arm", "depression", "asthma".

candidates.label: MedicalSignOrSymptom
candidates.comment: A medical condition representing any feature, objective or subjective, associated with a medical condition. Also called clinical manifestation, health indicator, disease feature. Examples: "pain", "fever", "fatigue", "rash", "nausea". Distinct from MedicalCondition, which is the underlying state itself.

candidates.label: MedicalConditionStage
candidates.comment: A medical intangible representing a specific stage of a medical condition. Also called disease stage, condition phase, severity level. Examples: "Stage IIIa cancer", "early-stage Alzheimer's", "acute phase of an infection".

candidates.label: InfectiousDisease
candidates.comment: An InfectiousDisease is a medical condition resulting from the presence of pathogenic microbial agents like viruses, bacteria, or fungi. Also called communicable disease, contagious illness, infection. Examples: influenza, COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis. Distinct from MedicalCondition, which is a broader category for any health problem.

candidates.label: MedicalContraindication
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing a condition or factor that serves as a reason to withhold a particular medical therapy. Also called contraindication, medical warning, therapy restriction. Examples: "pregnancy" for certain medications, "allergy to penicillin", "severe kidney disease".

types.embedding_query_text: Song: A musical composition, typically with lyrics, intended to be sung. Also called Track, Tune, Melody, Composition. Examples: Gnarly, Pinky Up, Gabriela.

chosen_type.label: MusicComposition
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org MusicComposition class represents the abstract musical work, which is the best fit for the OIE_TYPE 'Song' and its examples like 'Gnarly'.

candidates.label: MusicComposition
candidates.comment: A MusicComposition is a musical work, such as a song or symphony, that can be performed or recorded. Also called musical piece, song, score. Examples: Beethoven's 5th Symphony, 'Bohemian Rhapsody' by Queen, a jingle. Distinct from MusicRecording, which is a recorded performance of a composition.

candidates.label: SheetMusic
candidates.comment: Printed or written musical notation, as distinct from a performance or recording. Also called musical score, notation, music manuscript, song sheet. Examples: a piano concerto score, guitar tablature, a vocal sheet for a song, an orchestral score.

candidates.label: MusicRecording
candidates.comment: A MusicRecording, as a CreativeWork, is a recorded performance of a musical composition, usually a single song. Also called music track, song recording, audio track. Examples: 'Yesterday' by The Beatles (the recorded version), a single from an album, a demo track. Distinct from MusicComposition, which is the abstract musical work.

candidates.label: MusicAlbum
candidates.comment: A MusicAlbum, as a MusicPlaylist, is a collection of music tracks released together. Also called album, record album, studio album. Examples: 'Thriller' by Michael Jackson, 'Abbey Road' by The Beatles, a compilation album. Distinct from MusicRecording, which is usually a single song.

candidates.label: MusicPlaylist
candidates.comment: A MusicPlaylist, as a CreativeWork, is an ordered collection of music tracks. Also called playlist, music compilation, track list. Examples: a Spotify playlist, a radio station's daily playlist, a custom mix CD. Distinct from MusicAlbum, which is a formally released collection of tracks.

types.embedding_query_text: RecordLabel: A company that manages the production, manufacture, distribution, marketing, promotion, and enforcement of copyright for sound recordings and music videos. Also called Music Company, Label, Record Company, Music Publisher. Examples: HYBE x Geffen Records, the label.

chosen_type.label: RecordLabel
chosen_type.definition: A company that manages the production, manufacture, distribution, marketing, promotion, and enforcement of copyright for sound recordings and music videos.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class directly represents a 'RecordLabel' as an organization. Organization is the most appropriate parent.

candidates.label: MusicRelease
candidates.comment: A MusicRelease, as a MusicPlaylist, is a specific release of a music album, often with particular formats or editions. Also called album release, record release, music edition. Examples: a vinyl release of an album, a digital download version, a deluxe edition CD. Distinct from MusicAlbum, which is the conceptual collection of tracks.

candidates.label: MusicAlbumReleaseType
candidates.comment: MusicAlbumReleaseType is an enumeration describing the kind of release for a music album. Also called release format, album release category. Examples: Single, EP, Album. Distinct from MusicAlbumProductionType, which describes the content type.

candidates.label: MusicReleaseFormatType
candidates.comment: MusicReleaseFormatType is an enumeration describing the format of a music release. Also called release media type, recording format. Examples: CDFormat, DigitalAudioRecording, VinylFormat, CassetteFormat. Distinct from MusicAlbumReleaseType, which describes the kind of release (e.g., single, EP).

candidates.label: MusicAlbum
candidates.comment: A MusicAlbum, as a MusicPlaylist, is a collection of music tracks released together. Also called album, record album, studio album. Examples: 'Thriller' by Michael Jackson, 'Abbey Road' by The Beatles, a compilation album. Distinct from MusicRecording, which is usually a single song.

candidates.label: MusicAlbumProductionType
candidates.comment: MusicAlbumProductionType is an enumeration classifying a music album by its content type. Also called album type, production category. Examples: StudioAlbum, LiveAlbum, Soundtrack, CompilationAlbum. Distinct from MusicAlbumReleaseType, which describes the release format.

types.embedding_query_text: Activity: A specific action or task performed by an individual or group. Also called Task, Operation, Action, Undertaking. Examples: promotional activities, upcoming promotional activities.

chosen_type.label: Action
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org Action class is the most general and appropriate fit for the OIE_TYPE 'Activity' and the example 'promotional activities'.

candidates.label: PlayAction
candidates.comment: PlayAction is an Action involving playing, exercising, training, or performing for enjoyment, leisure, recreation, competition, or physical activity. Also called performing, engaging in recreation, exercising. Examples: playing a sport, performing music on stage, training for a marathon, engaging in a hobby. Distinct from ListenAction, which is consuming music; Distinct from WatchAction, which is consuming visual content.

candidates.label: OrganizeAction
candidates.comment: An OrganizeAction, as an Action, is the act of manipulating, administering, supervising, or controlling one or more objects. Also called arrange, manage, coordinate. Examples: organizing a conference, managing a project, arranging files on a computer. Distinct from CreateAction, which focuses on producing something new.

candidates.label: Action
candidates.comment: An Action is a fundamental schema.org type representing an activity performed by an agent, potentially involving objects, participants, locations, and instruments, and producing a result. Also called activity, operation, deed, event. Examples: Reading a book, buying groceries, sending an email, cooking dinner.

candidates.label: ScheduleAction
candidates.comment: The act of planning and allocating future actions, events, or tasks to specific time slots or spatial allocations. Also called planning, arranging, organizing, booking. Examples: scheduling a doctor's appointment, booking a meeting room, planning a project timeline, arranging a delivery. Distinct from ReserveAction, which implies making a reservation for a specific resource or service.

candidates.label: ExerciseAction
candidates.comment: ExerciseAction is a PlayAction representing the act of participating in exertive activity to improve health and fitness. Also called working out, physical activity, training. Examples: Going for a run, lifting weights, practicing yoga, swimming laps.

types.embedding_query_text: Fanbase: A collective group of admirers or enthusiasts for a particular person, group, or work. Also called Fans, Supporters, Admirers, Followers. Examples: EYEKONS.

chosen_type.label: PeopleAudience
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org PeopleAudience class is a specific type of audience composed of people, which accurately describes a 'Fanbase' like 'EYEKONS'.

candidates.label: Audience
candidates.comment: An Audience is an Intangible entity representing the specific group of people for whom an item or creative work is intended. Also called target group, readership, viewership, demographic. Examples: children, teenagers, medical professionals, general public, investors.

candidates.label: UserPlusOnes
candidates.comment: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of giving a "+1" endorsement, typically on Google+ or similar platforms. Also called user endorsement, +1, social recommendation. Examples: a user giving a +1 to a web page, endorsing a business, recommending content.

candidates.label: PeopleAudience
candidates.comment: A PeopleAudience, as an Audience, describes a set of characteristics belonging to people, e.g., who compose an item's target audience. Also called demographic group, target audience, human audience. Examples: 'adults aged 18-35', 'students', 'retirees'. Distinct from Audience, which is a broader category including non-human audiences.

candidates.label: UserReview
candidates.comment: A review or critique created by an end-user, such as a consumer or attendee, rather than a professional critic. Also called customer review, consumer feedback, public review. Examples: a customer's product review on an e-commerce site, a diner's restaurant review, an audience member's movie review. Distinct from CriticReview, which is a review written by a professional critic.

candidates.label: MemberProgramTier
candidates.comment: An intangible representing a specific tier within a loyalty or membership program. Also called membership level, loyalty tier, program status. Examples: "Gold Member", "Platinum Tier", "Basic Membership Level".

types.embedding_query_text: Profession: A paid occupation, especially one that involves prolonged training and a formal qualification. Also called Occupation, Career, Vocation, Job, Field. Examples: medical professionals.

chosen_type.label: Occupation
chosen_type.definition: The control of a country or region by a foreign military power.
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org Occupation class is a direct match for the OIE_TYPE 'Profession' and its definition, fitting 'medical professionals'.

candidates.label: Occupation
candidates.comment: An Occupation is a profession that may involve prolonged training and/or a formal qualification. Also called profession, job, career. Examples: doctor, engineer, teacher, artist. Distinct from Role, which describes a specific function within an organization or context.

candidates.label: ProfessionalService
candidates.comment: ProfessionalService is a LocalBusiness type for providers of specialized services. Also called expert service, specialized service. Examples: a legal service, an accounting service, a dental practice, an architectural firm. Distinct from Service, which is a broader concept of an intangible offering.

candidates.label: Physician
candidates.comment: A Physician, as a MedicalBusiness, is an individual doctor or a doctor's office considered as a MedicalOrganization. Also called doctor, medical practitioner, medical doctor. Examples: a general practitioner, a specialist physician, a family doctor's clinic. Distinct from Hospital, which is a larger medical facility.

candidates.label: Specialty
candidates.comment: Any branch of a field in which individuals develop specific expertise, typically through significant study and effort. Also called area of expertise, specialization, discipline, field. Examples: 'Cardiology' as a medical specialty, 'Corporate Law' as a legal specialty, 'Artificial Intelligence' as a computer science specialty.

candidates.label: MedicalSpecialty
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing any specific branch of medical science or practice, including clinical and allied health specialties. Also called medical field, clinical discipline, healthcare area. Examples: "Cardiology", "Pediatrics", "Oncology", "Physical Therapy", "Dentistry".

types.embedding_query_text: HealthRegimen: A prescribed course of diet, exercise, or other practices to promote health or recovery. Also called Treatment Plan, Wellness Program, Therapy, Health Protocol. Examples: extended rest, ongoing care.

chosen_type.label: LifestyleModification
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org LifestyleModification class, as a process of care involving changes to habits, best encompasses 'extended rest' and 'ongoing care' as parts of a health regimen.

candidates.label: LifestyleModification
candidates.comment: A LifestyleModification is a medical entity representing a process of care involving changes to diet, exercise, and other habits to improve a health condition. Also called health habit change, wellness intervention, behavioral therapy. Examples: a weight loss program, a smoking cessation plan, a stress reduction regimen.

candidates.label: DietarySupplement
candidates.comment: A product taken orally that contains dietary ingredients intended to supplement the diet, such as vitamins, minerals, or herbs. Also called Nutritional supplement, health supplement, vitamin, herbal remedy. Examples: Multivitamin pills, fish oil capsules, protein powder, ginseng extract. Distinct from Drug, which is primarily for treating, preventing, or diagnosing disease.

candidates.label: ExercisePlan
candidates.comment: An ExercisePlan is a CreativeWork representing a fitness-related activity designed for a specific health purpose, including routines or clinician-prescribed activities. Also called workout plan, fitness regimen, training program. Examples: A 30-day weight loss plan, a physical therapy exercise routine, a marathon training schedule, a yoga sequence.

candidates.label: Diet
candidates.comment: A creative work outlining a strategy for regulating food intake to achieve a specific health or fitness goal. Also called Eating plan, nutritional regimen, dietary program, meal plan. Examples: The Mediterranean diet, a ketogenic diet, a low-sodium diet, a vegan diet. Distinct from NutritionInformation, which provides factual data about food content.

candidates.label: MedicalTherapy
candidates.comment: A therapeutic medical procedure designed to prevent, treat, and cure human diseases and medical conditions. Also called medical treatment, healthcare intervention, therapy regimen. Examples: "pharmacotherapy", "behavioral therapy", "supportive therapy", "dialysis". Distinct from MedicalProcedure, which is a broader category including diagnostic procedures.

types.embedding_query_text: Date: A specific point or period in time. Also called Calendar Date, Day, Timepoint, Period. Examples: September, 07/08/2026.

chosen_type.label: Date
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org Date datatype is the most direct match for the OIE_TYPE 'Date' and the specific date example '07/08/2026'. 'September' can be interpreted as a date within that month.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

types.embedding_query_text: SocialMediaPlatform: An online service or site that facilitates interaction and content sharing among users. Also called Social Network, Online Community, Digital Platform, Networking Site. Examples: Instagram.

chosen_type.label: SocialMediaPlatform
chosen_type.definition: An online service or site that allows users to create and share content or to participate in social networking.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class directly represents a 'SocialMediaPlatform'. Service is a suitable parent as it describes an intangible offering.

candidates.label: DiscussionForumPosting
candidates.comment: A social media posting that is an entry or message within an online discussion forum. Also called Forum post, message board entry, thread reply, online discussion. Examples: A question posted on a tech support forum, a comment in a gaming community thread, a new topic started on a hobby board. Distinct from BlogPosting, which is typically a longer, standalone article on a blog.

candidates.label: SocialMediaPosting
candidates.comment: A creative work published on a social media platform, such as a blog post, tweet, or Facebook update. Also called social post, microblog post, status update, online share. Examples: a tweet from a celebrity, a Facebook status update, a blog post on Medium, an Instagram caption.

candidates.label: UserPlusOnes
candidates.comment: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of giving a "+1" endorsement, typically on Google+ or similar platforms. Also called user endorsement, +1, social recommendation. Examples: a user giving a +1 to a web page, endorsing a business, recommending content.

candidates.label: RuntimePlatform
candidates.comment: A specialized software environment providing the necessary infrastructure, libraries, and services for executing a program. Also called execution environment, software platform, runtime environment, operating system. Examples: Java Virtual Machine (JVM), Node.js runtime, .NET Common Language Runtime (CLR), Python interpreter.

candidates.label: DigitalPlatformEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration listing common technology platforms, used to specify where an action or content is available. Also called Technology platform, software platform, operating system, device type. Examples: iOS, Android, Web, Desktop, Console. Distinct from SoftwareApplication, which is the application itself, not the platform it runs on.

types.embedding_query_text: Year: A period of 365 or 366 days, divided into 12 months, starting from January 1st. Also called Annual Period, Calendar Year, Fiscal Year, Annum. Examples: 2023, last year.

chosen_type.label: CalendarYear
chosen_type.definition: A period of 365 or 366 days, divided into 12 months, starting from January 1st.
chosen_type.justification: Schema.org does not have a specific class for 'Year' as a temporal entity. Thing is the most general appropriate parent.

candidates.label: Season
candidates.comment: A distinct period within a media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called media season, series installment, broadcast season. Examples: 'Season 1 of Game of Thrones', 'The Fall 2023 radio season', 'Chapter 3 of a video game series'. Distinct from TVSeason, which is specifically for television broadcasts.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

candidates.label: TVSeason
candidates.comment: A distinct period of a television series, comprising multiple episodes, dedicated to TV broadcast and associated online delivery. Also called television season, broadcast season, show season. Examples: 'Season 1 of The Crown', 'The final season of Breaking Bad'. Distinct from Season, which is a more general media season.

types.embedding_query_text: Quantity: A specific amount or number of something. Also called Amount, Number, Count, Volume, Measure. Examples: six members, two, four members.

chosen_type.label: Quantity
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org Quantity datatype is a direct match for the OIE_TYPE 'Quantity' and its definition, covering numerical amounts like 'six members'.

candidates.label: Quantity
candidates.comment: Quantity is a data type representing measurable amounts such as distance, time, mass, or weight. Also called amount, measure, magnitude. Examples: '3 kg', '4 milligrams', '10 meters', '2 hours'.

candidates.label: Mass
candidates.comment: A quantity representing the amount of matter in an object, typically expressed with a unit of measure. Also called weight, bulk, quantity of matter. Examples: "5 kg", "10 pounds", "200 grams", "1 ton". Distinct from Quantity, which is a broader concept for any measurable amount.

candidates.label: Number
candidates.comment: Number is a data type representing numerical values. Also called numeric value, quantity, digit. Examples: 10, 3.14, -5, 1000000. Distinct from Text, which represents character strings.

candidates.label: Distance
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Distance represents a numerical value combined with a unit of length. Also called length, extent, span, separation. Examples: "10 km", "5 miles", "300 meters", "2 feet".

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

types.embedding_query_text: Award: A prize or other mark of recognition given in honor of an achievement. Also called Prize, Honor, Accolade, Distinction. Examples: Grammy Awards.

chosen_type.label: MusicEvent
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org MusicEvent class is the most specific and accurate fit for 'Grammy Awards', which is an event primarily featuring musical performances and awards.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: Certification
candidates.comment: An official and authoritative statement attesting to specific characteristics of a subject, issued by an independent body. Also called accreditation, credential, attestation, endorsement. Examples: ISO 9001 certification, Organic food certification, PMP certification, LEED certification.

candidates.label: MusicEvent
candidates.comment: A MusicEvent is an event primarily featuring musical performances. Also called concert, musical performance, gig. Examples: a rock concert, a classical symphony performance, a music festival. Distinct from PerformingArtsEvent, which includes broader performance types like theatre or dance.

candidates.label: WinAction
candidates.comment: The act of achieving victory or success in a competitive activity. Also called triumph, succeed, prevail. Examples: winning a race, winning a championship, winning an argument.

candidates.label: Statement
candidates.comment: A declaration or assertion about something, often a fact or an interesting piece of information. Also called assertion, declaration, factoid, claim. Examples: 'The Earth is round', 'Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius', 'The capital of France is Paris'. Distinct from Claim, which is used for more formal, verifiable assertions in fact-checking.

types.embedding_query_text: Threat: A statement of an intention to inflict pain, injury, damage, or other hostile action on someone in retribution for something done or not done. Also called Menace, Warning, Intimidation, Danger. Examples: online death threats, multiple online death threats.

chosen_type.label: Threat
chosen_type.definition: An event involving a stated intention to inflict harm or damage.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class directly represents a 'Threat'. Message is a suitable parent as a threat is a form of communication.

candidates.label: DisagreeAction
candidates.comment: A react action expressing a negative opinion or difference of opinion regarding an object, proposition, or theme. Also called Express disagreement, object to, dispute, dissent. Examples: Disagreeing with a political statement, objecting to a proposed plan, disputing a fact. Distinct from AgreeAction, which expresses positive sentiment or agreement.

candidates.label: DislikeAction
candidates.comment: A react action expressing a negative sentiment or disapproval towards an object, proposition, or theme. Also called Express dislike, disapprove of, show aversion, downvote. Examples: Disliking a movie, expressing disapproval of a policy, downvoting a comment online. Distinct from LikeAction, which expresses positive sentiment or approval.

candidates.label: Conversation
candidates.comment: A series of one or more messages exchanged between individuals or organizations on a specific topic. Also called discussion, dialogue, chat, discourse. Examples: An email thread, a text message exchange, a forum discussion, a spoken dialogue. Distinct from Comment, which is a single remark on an item.

candidates.label: Message
candidates.comment: A creative work representing a single communication from a sender to one or more recipients. Also called communication, dispatch, note, email. Examples: an email, a text message, a direct message on social media, a voicemail.

candidates.label: LoseAction
candidates.comment: The act of being defeated in a competitive activity or contest. Also called suffer defeat, be beaten, fail to win. Examples: losing a game, being defeated in an election, failing a competition. Distinct from AchieveAction, which is a broader category for actions that result in an outcome.

types.embedding_query_text: Event: A planned public or social occasion, or a noteworthy occurrence. Also called Occurrence, Incident, Happening, Occasion. Examples: debut.

chosen_type.label: Event
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org Event class is a direct match for the OIE_TYPE 'Event' and its definition, fitting 'debut' as a noteworthy occurrence.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: SocialEvent
candidates.comment: An event primarily focused on social interaction and entertainment. Also called party, gathering, social function, get-together. Examples: a birthday party, a wedding reception, a community picnic, a networking mixer.

candidates.label: DeliveryEvent
candidates.comment: An event representing the delivery of an item, typically a product or package. Also called Shipping event, package delivery, consignment event. Examples: A package arriving at its destination, a food delivery being completed, a furniture delivery appointment. Distinct from Order, which is the request for items, not the delivery itself.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: ScreeningEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving the public showing of a movie or other video content. Also called film screening, movie showing, video presentation, cinema event. Examples: a film festival screening, a premiere showing of a new movie, a public documentary viewing, a drive-in movie night.

types.embedding_query_text: Month: One of the twelve periods of time into which a year is divided. Also called Calendar Month, Period, Lunar Cycle. Examples: February.

chosen_type.label: Month
chosen_type.definition: One of the twelve periods of time into which a year is divided.
chosen_type.justification: Schema.org does not have a specific class for 'Month' as a temporal entity. Thing is the most general appropriate parent.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: Season
candidates.comment: A distinct period within a media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called media season, series installment, broadcast season. Examples: 'Season 1 of Game of Thrones', 'The Fall 2023 radio season', 'Chapter 3 of a video game series'. Distinct from TVSeason, which is specifically for television broadcasts.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: Periodical
candidates.comment: A Periodical, as a CreativeWorkSeries, is a publication issued in successive parts with numerical or chronological designations, intended to continue indefinitely. Also called serial publication, magazine, journal. Examples: The New Yorker magazine, a scholarly journal, a daily newspaper. Distinct from Book, which is a single, non-serial publication.

types.embedding_query_text: Age: The length of time that a person or thing has existed. Also called Lifespan, Duration, Years, Seniority. Examples: 23-year-old.

chosen_type.label: Duration
chosen_type.definition: The length of time that something continues or lasts.
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org Duration class, representing a period of time, is the best fit for 'Age' and the example '23-year-old'.

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: AdultOrientedEnumeration
candidates.comment: AdultOrientedEnumeration is an Enumeration of factors that make a product or content relevant or potentially restricted for adults only. Also called adult content classification, age restriction type, mature content indicator. Examples: `AdultSexualContent`, `ViolentContent`, `GamblingContent`.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: ShippingDeliveryTime
candidates.comment: A structured value providing details about the expected delivery times for product shipping. Also called delivery timeframe, estimated delivery, shipping lead time, transit time. Examples: 'ships in 1-2 business days', 'delivery by Friday', 'estimated 3-5 day transit'.

types.embedding_query_text: Nationality: The status of belonging to a particular nation by origin, birth, or naturalization. Also called Citizenship, Origin, Ethnicity, Country of Origin. Examples: Swiss, Filipino-American.

chosen_type.label: Nationality
chosen_type.definition: The status of belonging to a particular nation.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class directly represents 'Nationality' as a status. Intangible is a suitable parent for such a characteristic.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: StatusEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration type representing various status types or states. Also called status list, state types, condition enumeration. Examples: 'Active', 'Pending', 'Completed', 'Cancelled'.

candidates.label: Residence
candidates.comment: A Residence is a Place where a person lives. Also called home, dwelling, abode. Examples: a house, an apartment, a condominium, a dormitory room.

candidates.label: ReservationStatusType
candidates.comment: ReservationStatusType is a StatusEnumeration listing enumerated status values for a Reservation. Also called booking status, reservation state. Examples: ReservationConfirmed, ReservationPending, ReservationCancelled, ReservationHold.

candidates.label: CertificationStatusEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration defining the possible statuses of a certification. Also called certification state, approval status, credential status. Examples: Active, Inactive, Expired, Pending.

types.embedding_query_text: Communication: The imparting or exchanging of information by speaking, writing, or using some other medium. Also called Discussion, Dialogue, Exchange, Interaction. Examples: open and thoughtful conversations.

chosen_type.label: Conversation
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org Conversation class is a direct match for the OIE_TYPE 'Communication' when referring to 'open and thoughtful conversations'.

candidates.label: Conversation
candidates.comment: A series of one or more messages exchanged between individuals or organizations on a specific topic. Also called discussion, dialogue, chat, discourse. Examples: An email thread, a text message exchange, a forum discussion, a spoken dialogue. Distinct from Comment, which is a single remark on an item.

candidates.label: CommunicateAction
candidates.comment: The act of transmitting information to another person or entity through a specific medium. Also called communication, conveying information, interacting. Examples: Sending an email, making a phone call, giving a speech, writing a letter. Distinct from InteractAction, which is a broader category of actions involving interaction.

candidates.label: Message
candidates.comment: A creative work representing a single communication from a sender to one or more recipients. Also called communication, dispatch, note, email. Examples: an email, a text message, a direct message on social media, a voicemail.

candidates.label: ReplyAction
candidates.comment: ReplyAction is a CommunicateAction representing the act of responding to a question or message. Also called answering, responding, writing back. Examples: replying to an email, answering a question on a forum, responding to a text message, commenting on a social media post. Distinct from AskAction, which is the origin of a reply.

candidates.label: CommentAction
candidates.comment: The act of creating or submitting a comment about a particular subject. Also called commenting, posting a comment, providing feedback. Examples: Writing a review, replying to a forum post, adding a note to a document, leaving a social media comment. Distinct from Comment, which is the content itself.

types.embedding_query_text: NewsOrganization: An entity responsible for gathering, producing, and disseminating news and information to the public. Also called Media Outlet, News Agency, Broadcaster, Publisher. Examples: BBC News, bbc.com/news/articles/c4g305dz0y9o.

chosen_type.label: NewsMediaOrganization
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org NewsMediaOrganization class is a perfect match for the OIE_TYPE 'NewsOrganization' and the example 'BBC News'.

candidates.label: NewsMediaOrganization
candidates.comment: A NewsMediaOrganization is an organization that produces and disseminates news, such as a newspaper or TV station. Also called news agency, media outlet, journalistic organization. Examples: The New York Times, BBC News, CNN. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any type of organization.

candidates.label: GovernmentOrganization
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOrganization is an organization or agency that is part of a governmental body. Also called public sector entity, state agency, governmental body. Examples: Department of Defense, Environmental Protection Agency, National Institutes of Health, local city council.

candidates.label: ArchiveOrganization
candidates.comment: An ArchiveOrganization is a LocalBusiness that maintains, preserves, and typically provides public access to archival materials. Also called archives, historical society, records center, repository. Examples: National Archives, a university special collections library, a corporate archive, a local historical society.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: EducationalOrganization
candidates.comment: An EducationalOrganization is a CivicStructure that provides education. Also called learning institution, academic body, school. Examples: A university, a high school, a vocational college, a research institute.

types.embedding_query_text: Role: The function assumed or part played by a person or thing in a particular situation. Also called Position, Capacity, Function, Status. Examples: superstar, singer.

chosen_type.label: Role
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org Role class is a direct match for the OIE_TYPE 'Role' and its definition, fitting examples like 'superstar' and 'singer'.

candidates.label: Role
candidates.comment: Additional information describing a relationship or property, such as a person's function in an organization or a character played in a movie. Also called function, capacity, position, part. Examples: 'actor' role for a person in a film, 'member' role for a player on a sports team, 'author' role for a person on a book.

candidates.label: PerformanceRole
candidates.comment: A PerformanceRole, as a Role, is a role an entity plays in a theatrical performance, such as a movie or TV series. Also called acting role, character role, stage role. Examples: 'actor in a film', 'director of a play', 'musician in a concert'. Distinct from OrganizationRole, which is a role within an organization.

candidates.label: OrganizationRole
candidates.comment: An OrganizationRole, as a Role, describes a specific function or position within an organization. Also called organizational position, corporate role, job title. Examples: CEO, Marketing Manager, Board Member, Volunteer Coordinator. Distinct from Role, which is a broader category for any role.

candidates.label: EmployeeRole
candidates.comment: An EmployeeRole is an OrganizationRole describing the relationship of an individual as an employee within an organization. Also called job position, staff role, employment status. Examples: "Software Engineer" at Google, "Marketing Manager" at a startup, "Cashier" at a supermarket.

candidates.label: Occupation
candidates.comment: An Occupation is a profession that may involve prolonged training and/or a formal qualification. Also called profession, job, career. Examples: doctor, engineer, teacher, artist. Distinct from Role, which describes a specific function within an organization or context.

types.embedding_query_text: Assistance: The action of helping someone with a task or difficulty. Also called Help, Aid, Support, Cooperation. Examples: support, utmost support.

chosen_type.label: Service
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org Service class explicitly includes 'assistance' and 'support' in its definition, making it a good fit for the OIE_TYPE 'Assistance' and the example 'support'.

candidates.label: TipAction
candidates.comment: The act of voluntarily giving money to a beneficiary in appreciation for services rendered. Also called gratuity, tipping, giving a tip. Examples: leaving a tip for a waiter, tipping a taxi driver, giving a barber a gratuity.

candidates.label: BefriendAction
candidates.comment: An InteractAction representing the act of forming a mutual personal connection with someone. Also called make friends with, become friends, form a friendship. Examples: "Befriending a new colleague", "Making friends with a neighbor", "Forming a bond with a classmate". Distinct from FollowAction, which implies a non-reciprocal connection.

candidates.label: AuthorizeAction
candidates.comment: An AuthorizeAction is an AllocateAction representing the act of granting permission or approval for an object or action. Also called grant permission, approve, sanction, permit, allow. Examples: authorizing a payment, granting access to a file, approving a request, permitting a user to perform an action. Distinct from AuthenticateAction, which is about verifying identity, whereas AuthorizeAction is about granting permissions after identity is verified.

candidates.label: EndorseAction
candidates.comment: EndorseAction is a ReactAction where an agent approves, certifies, likes, supports, or sanctions an object. Also called approve, support, certify, sanction. Examples: Liking a post on social media, certifying a product as organic, endorsing a political candidate, giving a positive review.

candidates.label: Service
candidates.comment: An intangible offering provided by an organization, such as delivery, consulting, or repair. Also called offering, provision, assistance, support. Examples: a car repair service, a legal consulting service, a package delivery service, a web hosting service.

types.embedding_query_text: HealthOutcome: The result or consequence of a health intervention or condition. Also called Medical Result, Prognosis, Health Status, Recovery Status. Examples: recovery, full recovery.

chosen_type.label: MedicalOutcome
chosen_type.definition: The result or consequence of a medical condition, treatment, or intervention on a patient's health.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class directly represents a 'HealthOutcome' like 'recovery'. MedicalEntity is a suitable parent for a concept in the medical domain.

candidates.label: MedicalCondition
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing any condition of the human body that affects normal functioning, including diseases, injuries, disabilities, and disorders. Also called disease, illness, health disorder, ailment. Examples: "influenza", "diabetes", "a broken arm", "depression", "asthma".

candidates.label: MedicalRiskEstimator
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing any rule set or interactive tool used to estimate the risk of developing a complication or condition. Also called risk assessment tool, prognosis predictor, clinical risk model. Examples: a calculator for stroke risk, a scoring system for surgical complications. Distinct from MedicalRiskFactor, which is a single factor increasing risk.

candidates.label: MedicalProcedure
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing a process of care, invasive or non-invasive, used for diagnostic, therapeutic, preventive, or palliative purposes. Also called medical intervention, clinical procedure, healthcare process. Examples: "surgery", "biopsy", "vaccination", "physical therapy".

candidates.label: MedicalSignOrSymptom
candidates.comment: A medical condition representing any feature, objective or subjective, associated with a medical condition. Also called clinical manifestation, health indicator, disease feature. Examples: "pain", "fever", "fatigue", "rash", "nausea". Distinct from MedicalCondition, which is the underlying state itself.

candidates.label: MedicalIndication
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing a condition or factor that suggests the use of a medical therapy. Also called indication for treatment, therapeutic rationale, medical justification. Examples: "high blood pressure" as an indication for antihypertensive drugs, "fever" as an indication for antipyretics.

types.embedding_query_text: Action: The process of doing something, typically to achieve an aim. Also called Deed, Act, Movement, Operation. Examples: return.

chosen_type.label: ReturnAction
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org ReturnAction class is a specific type of action that directly matches the example 'return', which is more precise than the generic 'Action'.

candidates.label: ReturnAction
candidates.comment: ReturnAction is a TransferAction representing the act of returning something previously received or taken to its origin. Also called giving back, sending back, returning an item. Examples: returning a library book, sending back a purchased product, returning a rental car, giving back borrowed money.

candidates.label: FindAction
candidates.comment: FindAction is an Action representing the act of locating an object. Also called discover, locate, unearth. Examples: Finding a lost key, discovering a new species, locating a specific document, unearthing an artifact. Distinct from SearchAction, which is generally a precursor to FindAction.

candidates.label: WantAction
candidates.comment: The act of expressing a desire or wish for an object or outcome. Also called desire, wish for, covet. Examples: wanting a new car, desiring a specific job, wishing for peace.

candidates.label: SearchAction
candidates.comment: The act of looking for an object or information, often using a search engine or database. Also called searching, querying, looking up, seeking. Examples: typing a query into Google, searching for a file on a computer, looking up a contact in a directory. Distinct from FindAction, which is the result of a search, not the act itself.

candidates.label: TakeAction
candidates.comment: The act of gaining ownership of an object from an origin. Also called acquiring, receiving ownership, obtaining, getting. Examples: taking a book from a shelf, taking possession of a purchased item, taking a found object. Distinct from GiveAction, which is the reciprocal act of transferring ownership. Distinct from ReceiveAction, which does not necessarily imply ownership transfer.

types.embedding_query_text: Audience Examples: fans.

chosen_type.label: PeopleAudience
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org PeopleAudience class is a specific type of audience composed of people, which accurately describes 'fans'.

candidates.label: Audience
candidates.comment: An Audience is an Intangible entity representing the specific group of people for whom an item or creative work is intended. Also called target group, readership, viewership, demographic. Examples: children, teenagers, medical professionals, general public, investors.

candidates.label: PeopleAudience
candidates.comment: A PeopleAudience, as an Audience, describes a set of characteristics belonging to people, e.g., who compose an item's target audience. Also called demographic group, target audience, human audience. Examples: 'adults aged 18-35', 'students', 'retirees'. Distinct from Audience, which is a broader category including non-human audiences.

candidates.label: MedicalAudience
candidates.comment: An audience type representing target groups for medical web pages. Also called healthcare audience, patient demographic, medical readership. Examples: "patients", "healthcare professionals", "medical researchers", "general public interested in health".

candidates.label: EducationalAudience
candidates.comment: An EducationalAudience is an Audience specifically targeted for educational content or programs. Also called student group, learner demographic, academic audience. Examples: K-12 students, university undergraduates, adult learners, professional development participants.

candidates.label: BusinessAudience
candidates.comment: A BusinessAudience is an Audience defined by characteristics relevant to businesses, such as their industry, size, or role in the value chain. Also called B2B audience, corporate audience, professional audience. Examples: small business owners, IT managers, marketing executives, manufacturing companies. Distinct from PeopleAudience, which targets individual consumers.
